incidents.victim: Mackay Sugar (Australia's 2nd-largest sugar producer)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into the company's IT environment followed by a ransomware/data-theft extortion claim on a dark web leak site.
incidents.impact: Two of three sugar mills (Racecourse and Farleigh) have been shut since June 10, halting harvesting across Queensland's Mackay cane region; the company is restoring systems and investigating what data was accessed.

incidents.victim: FortiGate firewall operators worldwide (~73,932 devices, 194 countries)
incidents.attacker: Russia — Russian-speaking criminal group (mass credential theft)
incidents.vector: 'FortiBleed' dataset of valid admin and SSL-VPN credentials assembled via ~1.16 billion credential attempts, interception of VPN auth hashes, and offline GPU-cluster cracking of exported FortiGate config files.
incidents.impact: Tens of thousands of FortiGate firewalls across government, telecom, finance, healthcare, manufacturing and critical infrastructure exposed; researchers validated sampled credentials as authentic and confirmed Active Directory access. Affected orgs must rotate credentials immediately.

incidents.victim: European Commission (Europa.eu platform on AWS)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (TeamPCP; data later listed by ShinyHunters)
incidents.vector: Initial access via the Trivy supply-chain compromise, then misuse of a secret Amazon API key to access the Commission's AWS account.
incidents.impact: CERT-EU attributed a March 19 breach to TeamPCP; about 92 GB of compressed data (names, email addresses, some email content) tied to 42 internal clients and 29+ EU entities was taken and surfaced on ShinyHunters' dark web site.

incidents.victim: LiteLLM users (open-source AI gateway package on PyPI)
incidents.vector: Malicious versions (1.82.7, 1.82.8) of the widely used LiteLLM Python package published to PyPI using valid publishing access, likely via a compromised maintainer account.
incidents.impact: Poisoned packages (~3M daily downloads) were live for at least two hours and designed to steal cloud credentials, API keys and crypto wallets and install a persistent downloader; potential to affect tens of thousands of corporate environments, including AI firm Mercor.

incidents.victim: Red Hat software distribution users (developers/customers)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain worm (Mini Shai-Hulud 'Miasma' variant)
incidents.vector: A compromised GitHub account was used to push credential-stealing malware (a self-propagating Shai-Hulud worm variant) into Red Hat's distribution pipeline.
incidents.impact: 32 packages downloaded ~117,000 times per week were tainted before Red Hat pulled them; the company says no customer action is required. Derived from TeamPCP's open-sourced worm code, now spawning copycats.

incidents.victim: Mastra npm ecosystem users (developers, CI/CD pipelines)
incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account to publish 140+ poisoned packages across the mastra/@mastra scopes, introducing a malicious dayjs typosquat ('easy-day-js') whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper.
incidents.impact: Microsoft attributes the compromise with high confidence to North Korean actor Sapphire Sleet; any workstation or CI/CD pipeline that ran npm install/update fetched a hidden second-stage payload. Packages removed and publish access revoked, but installed hosts remain at risk.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiSandbox appliance operators
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of critical FortiSandbox flaws CVE-2026-39808 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-39813 (path traversal), disclosed in April, plus attempts against CVE-2026-25089.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed 49 exploitation events from 11 IPs over six days, originating from nine countries; the recon/verification activity signals the early stage of a likely larger wave against trusted security appliances. Not yet in CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: Open-source software supply chain (npm, PyPI, RubyGems ecosystems)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — self-propagating supply chain worm (Shai-Hulud variants)
incidents.vector: Shai-Hulud worm variants exploiting GitHub design flaws; GitHub reportedly closed two formal vulnerability reports from Deep Specter as ineligible despite ongoing exploitation.
incidents.impact: Deep Specter confirmed 516 malicious packages live across five ecosystems, 3,000+ affected GitHub repositories and 200+ compromised developer accounts — figures it calls a floor. Linked to breaches at the European Commission, Mercor, LiteLLM, GitHub and Red Hat.

incidents.victim: Healthcare, manufacturing, legal and other sensitive-data sectors
incidents.vector: Double-extortion ransomware delivered via spear-phishing, broker-supplied valid credentials, and exploitation of known flaws (Citrix Bleed 2 CVE-2025-5777, SimpleHelp CVE-2024-57727, NetScaler CVE-2023-3519).
incidents.impact: Acronis reports the INC RaaS group has claimed 800+ victims since 2023, deliberately hitting sectors where disruption forces fast payment; prior victims include NHS Dumfries & Galloway and Alder Hey Children's Hospital.

incidents.victim: Silver Fox cybercrime group members (China-based)
incidents.vector: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces tied to the Silver Fox trojan, distributed via malspam and fake download sites to deploy infostealers and the AtlasRAT/ValleyRAT remote-access trojans.
incidents.impact: Disruption of China's largest and most active domestic cybercrime group; arrests spanned developers, phishing-site operators and affiliates, including the malware's primary author. The group had recently begun expanding beyond Chinese-speaking targets.

incidents.victim: Web users via compromised WordPress sites
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware/data extortion (Rapid Brigantine / Vice Society)
incidents.vector: The 'Lorem Ipsum' shellcode loader pivoted from Trojanized Microsoft Teams installers to ClickFix lures hosted on compromised WordPress sites after Microsoft dismantled the Fox Tempest malware-signing service.
incidents.impact: BlueVoyant links the campaign to financially motivated group Rapid Brigantine (aka Vanilla Tempest / Vice Society), tied to Rhysida, BlackCat, Zeppelin and Quantum Locker ransomware; the ClickFix shift broadens the victim pool to anyone browsing the poisoned sites.

incidents.victim: US public and private medical research community
incidents.vector: China-nexus actor UNC6508 abused Google Workspace compliance rules and exploited REDCap research-platform vulnerabilities for intelligence collection.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence reports a sophisticated campaign targeting AI, cyber, medical and national-defense research data across the public and private medical community.

incidents.victim: Arch Linux users (AUR community packages)
incidents.vector: Attackers abused the AUR 'adopt' mechanism to seize 1,900+ orphaned community packages and inject a malicious npm/Bun install step that downloaded a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: Affected users got a rootkit plus a credential harvester collecting browser, Electron-app and developer secrets; victims are urged to rotate all passwords/tokens before removing persistence. Hijack attempts were still ongoing at time of reporting.

incidents.victim: Higher-education institutions worldwide (100+ orgs, incl. University of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools zero-day CVE-2026-35273, an unauthenticated RCE that allows server takeover; Oracle issued mitigation guidance but no patch.
incidents.impact: Mandiant says attacks date to at least May 27 and potentially compromised 100+ organizations, 68% in higher education; ShinyHunters is naming victims and leaking data, with University of Nottingham confirming significant student-data theft. Campaign still active.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (1,000+ orgs globally)
incidents.vector: DOJ secured a guilty plea from Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko, who admitted developing malware used in Conti attacks and holding data on 12 victims.
incidents.impact: Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to wire-fraud conspiracy and faces up to 20 years; Conti hit 1,000+ victims across 47 US states and ~31 countries and extorted $150M+. Prosecutors cited $634K taken from two Tennessee victims, including a compromised sheriff's department and EMS.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Sentry mobile gateway
incidents.vector: Exploitation of max-severity (CVSS 10) OS command-injection flaw CVE-2026-10520 using a public proof-of-concept, within 24 hours of disclosure, enabling unauthenticated root RCE.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver observed mass exploitation attempts and spotted 19 vulnerable instances, at least two already backdoored; unpatched Sentry instances are likely compromised. A second flaw, CVE-2026-10523 (auth bypass, CVSS 9.9), was disclosed alongside.

incidents.victim: US security clearance holders (current & former)
incidents.vector: Thirteen fake 'consulting company' websites used social-engineering lures offering easy income to recruit clearance holders into revealing classified or sensitive information.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized the 13 domains backed by suspected Chinese agents that targeted current and former clearance holders with access to classified US government information.

incidents.victim: WhatsApp users targeted by spyware
incidents.vector: A spear-phishing operation lured targeted WhatsApp users into clicking a malicious link leading to an external site, in alleged violation of a US court injunction barring NSO from targeting Meta's platforms.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted the new NSO campaign and filed to hold the (US-sanctioned) Israeli spyware firm in contempt, urging lawmakers to keep sanctions in place; researchers warn NSO's weakened legal status has made it more reckless.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager customers
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of zero-day CVE-2026-20245, a validation-error flaw in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager allowing authenticated/local attackers to execute commands as root; no patch yet available.
incidents.impact: The seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year; Cisco observed limited cases where exploitation pushed configuration changes to edge devices. Exploitation requires existing credentials, often obtained via earlier zero-days CVE-2026-20182/20127.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of PAN-OS authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-0257 in the GlobalProtect portal/gateway, allowing attackers to circumvent controls and initiate VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed an unidentified actor probing GlobalProtect, with only a small portion of devices establishing VPN sessions and no post-access lateral movement yet identified. Added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29.

incidents.victim: Check Point Remote Access VPN / Mobile Access customers
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of critical authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-50751 (CVSS 9.3) in IKEv1-configured VPN deployments, letting attackers establish a VPN session without valid credentials.
incidents.impact: Exploited in the wild since early May against a few dozen organizations globally; Check Point confirmed one case where post-exploitation activity was tied to a Qilin ransomware affiliate. A related MitM flaw, CVE-2026-50752, was disclosed alongside.

incidents.victim: US legal, professional and financial services firms
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft extortion (Silent Ransom / Luna Moth)
incidents.vector: Vishing and IT-support impersonation to trick staff into screen-sharing and installing legitimate RMM tools, escalating in some cases to in-person office intrusions and USB-based data theft.
incidents.impact: Mandiant (tracking the group as UNC3753) reports dozens of organizations targeted Jan-May 2026, with some intrusions moving from initial contact to data exfiltration and ransom demands in under an hour.
